_README: Out-of-archive CASE DESCRIPTIONS for eval/run_narrative_eval.py: the same style as
the generated narratives (40-150 words, first person where natural, facts + each
side's claim + what the courts below held), for situations NOT decided by any of
the 11 judgments indexed on 2026-10-03. The right behaviour today is to show
nothing; showing a judgment as 'high' (Strong match) is the worst failure.
domain 'near' = a Pakistani-law situation that shares vocabulary with the indexed
judgments (pre-emption, maintenance, compulsory retirement, Senate disqualification,
rent, tax, cheque, bail, NAB, khula, regularisation, promotion ...). These are the
hard negatives. Every near-domain row has verify_at_scale: true: at 1,000 / 3,000
Supreme Court judgments a judgment deciding that very situation may exist. The
runner therefore reports a near-domain row that retrieves a judgment as a
CANDIDATE POSITIVE in eval/labels/narrative_negative_candidates.json, not as a
failure. A human decides: relabel it as a positive (move it into a dataset with
relevant {pdf_id: 2}) or keep it negative by setting verify_at_scale false.
domain 'far' = foreign law or no court case at all. verify_at_scale: false; these
stay negatives forever and retrieving anything is a failure.
Wording deliberately avoids the facts of the 11 indexed judgments (dower land and
revenue entries, evacuee land sale, family-settlement limitation, the post-office
clerk, the Shezan trade mark, embassy local staff, police lower-school seniority,
the Barkhan re-poll, the NA-266 rigging petition, Sindh contract regularisation,
Peshawar municipal property). A few rows (n-reg-*, n-promo-*) are intentionally
close to an indexed judgment's subject: they test whether a similar-but-different
situation is shown as a 'Strong match'.

negatives.query: My client bought eight kanals of agricultural land in a village near Sahiwal. Within a few weeks a neighbouring owner sued for pre-emption, saying his land adjoins ours and he made the required demands as soon as he learned of the sale. We say he never made the first demand in front of witnesses and the notice he sent was late. The trial court dismissed his suit but the appellate court decreed it.

My uncle sold his share of our family fields to an outsider without telling us. We wanted to buy it ourselves because we share the water channel and the boundary. By the time we went to court they said we had waited too long and had not announced our claim properly. Can we still get the land back?

I was married for six years and have two daughters. My husband threw me out of the house and stopped all support. I went to the Family Court for maintenance for myself and the children and for return of my dowry articles, jewellery and furniture. The Family Court granted everything, but on appeal the district judge cut the children's maintenance in half and said the jewellery was not proved.

My client is a father who was ordered to pay maintenance to his minor son at an amount he cannot afford on a clerk's salary. The mother hid that she remarried and the child lives with his grandparents. The Family Court refused to reduce the amount and the High Court dismissed his writ petition saying it would not reassess evidence.

I cannot live with my husband any more because he beats me and keeps me away from my parents. I asked the court to end the marriage. He says he will only agree if I give back the gold and the money he gave at the wedding. The judge ended the marriage but ordered me to return everything. Is that fair?

The wife filed for dissolution of marriage on the basis of khula alleging cruelty and non-payment of maintenance. My client, the husband, says she left the home on her own and is being influenced by her family. The Family Court dissolved the marriage at the pre-trial stage after reconciliation failed, without recording evidence, and the High Court refused to interfere.

After my wife died, her mother took our five-year-old son and refuses to return him. I applied to the Guardian Judge for custody. The grandmother says I have remarried and my new wife will not look after the boy. The Guardian Judge gave custody to the grandmother with weekly visits for me, and my appeal was dismissed.

I was an assistant professor of chemistry at a public university. A committee accused me of copying parts of my research paper from another author and the syndicate compulsorily retired me. I say the committee never gave me the report or a chance to cross-examine anyone. The provincial service tribunal said it had no jurisdiction over university teachers and the High Court dismissed my petition.

My father taught at a government school for twenty-two years. They sent him home early on retirement, saying he had been absent for months, but he was in hospital after a heart attack and had sent the papers. The department ignored his doctors and the higher authority agreed with them. We want his job back or full pension.

My client won a Senate seat from the province on a technocrat seat. A rival candidate complained that he still held British citizenship when he filed his nomination papers. We produced the renunciation certificate, which is dated after the nomination but before polling. The Election Commission de-notified him and the High Court dismissed his writ petition.

A member of the provincial assembly did not declare an apartment in Dubai and a bank account in his nomination papers. His opponent sought a declaration that he is not honest and should be disqualified for life. The returned member says the property belongs to his wife and was disclosed in her tax return. The High Court disqualified him.

I filed nomination papers for chairman of a union council in the local government elections. The returning officer rejected them because the electricity company said I owed unpaid bills. I had paid the bill two days earlier and showed the receipt. The appellate authority upheld the rejection and the High Court said the election process could not be interrupted.

My client has run a shop in a Karachi market as a tenant for thirty years. The new owner filed an ejectment application saying he needs the shop in good faith for his son's business and that rent was not paid for four months. We deposited the rent in court after the landlord refused the money order. The Rent Controller and the appellate court ordered eviction.

I own a small house and the family living in it stopped paying me two years ago. They now say they bought the house from my late father through a paper I have never seen, so they are not tenants at all. The rent court told them to pay or leave but they keep appealing. How do I get my house back?

The tax authorities said my client's textile company claimed input tax on invoices from suppliers who were blacklisted as fake. They issued a show-cause notice years later and created a demand with default surcharge and penalty. We say the suppliers were active on the system when we bought from them. The appellate tribunal upheld the demand.

I am a doctor with a private clinic. The income tax office amended my assessment and added unexplained investment because I bought a plot in my son's name. I proved the money came from my agricultural income which is exempt. The commissioner appeals agreed with me, but the tribunal reversed and the High Court answered the reference against me.

I lent my friend money for his shop and he gave me a cheque. When I took it to the bank it bounced. I complained to the police and they arrested him, but now he says the cheque was only a guarantee and he never owed me anything. The magistrate let him off. What can I do?

negatives.topic: summary suit on a dishonoured cheque
negatives.query: My client sued on three dishonoured cheques under the summary procedure for recovery of money. The defendant applied for leave to defend saying the cheques were signed blank as security for a partnership that never started. The trial court refused leave because he did not deposit the amount, decreed the suit, and the High Court upheld the decree.

My client is accused in a murder case registered two days after the occurrence. He is named only for raising a lalkara, not for firing. The co-accused who allegedly fired has been granted bail. The medical evidence does not match the eyewitness account. The trial court and the High Court refused post-arrest bail saying the offence falls within the prohibitory clause.

My brother was caught by police who say they found a bag of hashish in his car. He says it was not his car and the police made up the story because of a fight with an officer. He has been in jail for a year and the trial has not started. The courts keep refusing to release him.

My client was convicted for transporting four kilograms of heroin and sentenced to life imprisonment. The sample was sent to the chemical examiner after eleven days and the officer who kept it in the malkhana was never examined. The High Court dismissed the appeal saying the delay was not fatal. We say the safe custody chain is broken.

A young man was convicted of murdering his cousin over a land quarrel and sentenced to death mainly on the victim's statement in hospital before he died. The defence says the victim was unconscious, no doctor certified that he was fit to speak and the statement was written by a police official. The High Court confirmed the death sentence.

My son was killed by his wife's brothers because they disapproved of the marriage. Later the killers' family pressured my other relatives to forgive them and a compromise deed was filed. I never agreed. The trial court accepted the compromise and acquitted them, and the High Court refused to apply the law that prevents compromise in such killings.

My client, a retired official of a development authority, was named in an accountability reference for owning plots and a house beyond his known income. The investigation ignored that the property was inherited from his father and bought from his wife's salary. The accountability court convicted him and the High Court dismissed his appeal, relying on the investigating officer's chart.

I was arrested by the accountability bureau in a case about a housing society. Under pressure in custody I agreed to a plea bargain and paid a large amount, which disqualified me from my government job. I later applied to withdraw the plea bargain saying it was not voluntary. The court refused and my department dismissed me from service.

The provincial government acquired my clients' orchards for a motorway and paid compensation at the average price of the last year. We say the land is next to a city and was being sold for residential plots at five times that rate. The referee court enhanced the compensation, but the High Court reduced it again on the government's appeal.

negatives.topic: specific performance of agreement to sell
negatives.query: I agreed to buy a house in Rawalpindi and paid half the price as earnest money. The seller then refused to execute the sale deed because prices went up, and said the agreement was forged. I sued for specific performance. The trial court decreed my suit, but the appellate court held that I had not shown I was ready with the balance money and dismissed it.

Before he died my father supposedly gave all his property to my brothers as a gift. My sisters and I were left out. We think the papers were made when he was very ill and could not understand anything. Our brothers say he did it willingly in front of witnesses. The lower courts believed them. Can we still claim our share?

My husband was a government teacher who died in service. The accounts office refused to give me the family pension and the benevolent fund because his parents also applied and claimed I was divorced before his death. I have the marriage certificate and no divorce was ever registered. The department kept the case pending for years and the tribunal dismissed my appeal as time-barred.

I am a section officer in a provincial secretariat. The selection board deferred my promotion twice because of two adverse annual reports that were never communicated to me. Officers below me were promoted. My representation was not decided. The service tribunal held that promotion is not a vested right and dismissed my appeal.

My client was transferred from the education department to the revenue department as an assistant on his own request. The revenue department placed him at the bottom of the seniority list from the date of transfer, ignoring his earlier service. He says his posts were equivalent. The tribunal agreed with the department and dismissed his appeal.

I have taught as a contract lecturer at a government college in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for nine years, renewed every year. A new law regularised employees on contract, but the department says lecturers must be selected by the Public Service Commission and refused to include us. The High Court dismissed our petitions saying policy matters are for the government.

A bank filed a recovery suit against my client's rice mill for a running finance facility, claiming markup for years after the facility expired. We say the bank charged compound markup that the agreement did not allow and sold our pledged stock without notice. The banking court decreed the full amount and the High Court dismissed our appeal.

My new car was stolen from outside my house and I had full insurance. The insurance company refused to pay saying I left the keys inside and did not report quickly enough. I reported it the same night. The insurance tribunal sided with the company. Do I have any chance in a higher court?

I worked as a machine operator in a cement factory for fourteen years and was a union office-bearer. The management dismissed me for allegedly slowing down work, without any proper inquiry. The labour court ordered reinstatement with back benefits, but the labour appellate tribunal set that aside saying I had been given a show-cause notice.

The power distribution company sent my flour mill a detection bill of several million rupees, alleging that the meter was tampered with. No one from my side was present when they checked the meter and the laboratory report came months later. The electric inspector cancelled the bill but the company went to court and the civil judge restored it.

I complained to the Ombudsperson that my manager at a public sector company harassed me with messages and threatened my contract. The Ombudsperson found him guilty and ordered his removal. He appealed to the Governor, who set aside the finding saying the complaint was filed late. The High Court upheld the Governor's order.

Customs officers seized my client's jeep at a checkpoint saying it was smuggled and its chassis number was tampered. He bought it through an open auction and has the registration documents. The adjudicating officer ordered confiscation with an option to pay a fine, the appellate tribunal upheld it, and the High Court dismissed the reference.

Some men broke into my shop, beat my son and took cash, and everyone in the street saw it. The local police station refused to write a report because one of them is related to a politician. I went to the sessions judge who told the police to register the case, but the High Court cancelled that order.

My daughter applied for admission to a public medical college on a seat reserved for a backward district. The admission committee gave the seat to a student whose domicile we believe was obtained falsely. Her marks were higher than the selected candidate. The High Court dismissed our petition saying the admission session had already started.

My client was the lowest bidder for a road construction contract tendered by a district government. The contract was awarded to a higher bidder after the evaluation committee changed the experience criteria. The grievance committee dismissed our complaint and the High Court held that the work had already started and refused to cancel the contract.

A newspaper published a story calling me corrupt and claiming I took bribes as a municipal engineer. An inquiry later cleared me. I sued the newspaper and the reporter for damages. The district judge awarded damages, but the High Court set the decree aside saying the story was published in good faith and in the public interest.

I rented a flat in Manchester for two years. When I moved out the landlord kept my whole deposit, saying I damaged the carpets and walls, and he never put the deposit in a government protection scheme. The county court awarded me the deposit back but refused the penalty of three times the deposit.

I worked as an assistant manager at a fast-food chain in Texas for three years, often sixty hours a week. They classified me as exempt so I never got overtime, although I mostly cooked and cleaned like the crew. The federal district court granted summary judgment for the company and I want to appeal.

I bought a used car from a dealer in Munich and the gearbox failed after five months. The dealer says it was my driving and refuses to repair it for free, even though I was told a defect in the first year is assumed to have been there at sale. Who is right?

My client is a software developer who released a library under an open-source licence. A California start-up used it in a commercial product and refused to publish its source code as the licence requires. The federal court said the licence was only a contract and dismissed the copyright claim, leaving a small damages claim.

I am a professional footballer. My club in Portugal stopped paying my salary for four months, so I terminated my contract and signed with a club in Spain. My old club claims I left without just cause and wants compensation. The players' status chamber ruled against me and banned me for four months.

The roots of my neighbour's huge maple tree have cracked my driveway and the foundation of my garage here in Ontario. He refuses to cut it down or pay for the repairs and says the tree was there before my house was built. My insurance will not cover it. What are my options?

I flew from Dubai to Toronto with a connection in London and my suitcase never arrived. The airline offered me a small fixed amount, far less than what my clothes, laptop and gifts were worth, saying international rules limit what they must pay. Can I claim the full value?

My husband and I divorced in British Columbia after twenty years. The family court divided our house equally but refused to divide his workplace pension, saying I had signed a prenuptial agreement. I say I signed it the night before the wedding without a lawyer. The appeal court upheld the agreement.

My mother had a routine knee replacement in a private hospital in Sydney and developed a serious infection because, we believe, the surgical instruments were not properly sterilised. She lost the leg. The hospital says infection is a known risk she accepted in the consent form. The state court dismissed our negligence claim for lack of expert evidence.

My client owns a United States patent on a method of unlocking a phone by swiping a pattern. A large manufacturer sells phones using a similar gesture. The jury found infringement and awarded damages, but the judge set the verdict aside holding the patent invalid as obvious in light of earlier devices.

I run a small home business in Leeds making custom wedding cakes and post my designs online. Another baker copied my most popular designs exactly, even using my photos in her adverts, and customers think she is me. She says you cannot own a cake design. Can I stop her?

A cryptocurrency exchange registered in Singapore froze my account holding about forty thousand dollars of coins, saying it needed to verify my identity again. I sent every document they asked for, but after eight months they still refuse to release the funds and their terms say disputes go to arbitration in Singapore.
